Synopsis:
Non-critpath. Two giant spiders trap the player. The one that shoots the web is female. Her companion is her brother.  The player has a chance to convince the spiders they are friendly, setting the spiders loose on the goblins in the camp above.

Cluster Contexts:
- GOB_SpiderNest_Spiders.json: The party has fallen into a pit and is confronted by two giant spiders: a web‑shooting female and her companion, who is her brother. Both are defensive, hungry, and ready to attack — one may even be visibly excited at the idea of eating the party. Off‑screen the game resolves a hidden "calm or provoke" check when the player uses nonthreatening gestures or words; success can settle the spiders (or prompt a verbal warning), while failure triggers aggression. If the player soothes them, they can be coaxed out of the pit and set loose to hunt the goblins in the camp above.
- GOB_SpiderNest_Spiders_CantSpeak.json: Two giant spiders trap the player. Normally, the player has a chance to convince the spiders they are friendly, setting the spiders loose on the goblins in the camp above. But in this case, the player is unable to speak and can't make their case.
- GOB_GiantSpider_Tiny.json: The party has just entered a pit where a captive giant spider (labeled here as the Smaller Giant Spider) is confined; it is defensive and prepared to attack anyone who looks like a threat. Off-screen, the players have the chance to use non‑threatening gestures or dialogue (for example, holding up their hands or claiming they mean no harm) and the game resolves a hidden check that can succeed or fail. In successful outcomes the spider calms or even speaks a warning about its territory instead of attacking; on failure it reacts aggressively. The three excerpts show different possible immediate responses, not an exhaustive list of outcomes.
- UND_SpiderFight_FourWay.json: In this dialogue, Lur Xanta is trying to convince the other 3 to leave with her to join the cult of Lolth.Player can help her convince them, or fail to do so and they will attack Lur Xanta for being disloyal.This dialogue has 2 outcomes:AGGRO: Lur Jox (or another spider) attacks Lur Xanta, killing her in one shot. (via gameplay - not cine)PEACEFUL: Lur Xanta convinces the other 3 to follow her into the Underdark-- they are leaving to somewhere new.Lur Xanta is fantatical and somewhat learned. The other 3 are a bit more simple.
- SCL_Drider_CaravanStart.json: Dialog featuring a goblin and half-orc. Triggers the start of the caravan escort with the Drider appearing.The Drider is male, half-drow elf and half spider (bottom half). He carries a magical lantern to ward off the shadows

Sample 1:
- Narrator: *The spider seems poised to attack, but she hesitates, tapping her claws as if trying to communicate.* (node 22)
- Narrator: *The other spider echoes her.* || [context] CinematicNodeContext: *The other spider echoed her, tapping his claws gleefully.* (node 43)
- Player: Clap your hands together, mimicking her movements. (node 33)
- : True (node 1)
- Narrator: *The spider relaxes slightly, but you feel her hunger - and fear - beneath the surface.* (node 38)
- Player: Usher her toward the door. (node 32)

Sample 2:
- Larger Giant Spider: Yes, my desire. Closer, my sweet! || [context] NodeContext: Excited, drooling with desire to eat us. (node 11)
- Larger Giant Spider: I will wrap you, and bind you, and bite you, and eat you. || [context] NodeContext: Excited, almost to herself, thinking about how she'll eat us (node 25)
- Player: You should eat a goblin instead. They're delicious. (node 29)
- : True (node 12)

context: The party has fallen into a non‑critical pit and been confronted by two giant spiders: a web‑shooting female and her companion, who is her brother. Both are defensive, hungry, and ready to attack (one is even visibly excited at the thought of eating the party). Off‑screen the game resolves a hidden “calm or provoke” check when the player uses nonthreatening gestures or words; success will soothe the spiders (they may issue a warning and can be coaxed out of the pit), while failure triggers aggression. In some variations the player cannot speak and so cannot make a verbal case; in successful examples shown the player uses mimicry or suggests the spiders eat the goblins in the camp above instead.
